title: Current and next-year drought slopes for desert bird richness did not clearly differ in two US samples in 1998-2021
abstract: We tested whether the annual drought slope for recorded bird richness was more negative for current than next-year weather. Two US desert bird samples used 301 and 254 matched surveys in 1998-2009 and 2010-2021. Models controlled route, year, survey date and land cover. Current-minus-next-year slopes were +1.020 and -0.515 species per unit lower SPEI-12. Both four-test intervals included zero, as did both current slopes. Planned sensitivity checks also left the current slopes and direct contrasts uncertain. This does not show that drought has no effect. The samples share routes and source records with prior work. Future-survey selection, few year clusters, unknown exact climate windows and remaining detection bias limit inference. No causal effect, pollution effect or regional replication is established. Code, source hashes, aggregate results, a figure and numerical checks support reproduction.

display.caption: Current and next-year dryness slopes and their direct difference. All main intervals include zero. Intervals use the four-test multiplier; next-year coefficients are descriptive.
